sentences.text: The complainant has filed the complaint under Section 223 of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhitha 2023 against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

2. The brief case of the complainant is as under:
That the complainant is a Non Banking Financial company engaged in the business of extending financial credit facilities in the form of various loans to the borrowers.

During the course of business, the accused approached the complainant company for availing financial assistance towards purchasing commercial vehicles / equipment by assuring to abide by the terms and conditions.

On the assurance and promises made by the accused, the complainant company sanctioned loan of Rs.24,43,000/- towards purchase of commercial vehicle/ equipment, accordingly loan agreement bearing No.
LNVEN0007389 was executed between the complainant and the accused.
As per said agreement, the accused has undertaken to make payments as per the repayment schedule.
In view of default in repayment of loan installments, the complainant company terminated and recalled the outstanding loan amount.
Subsequently, the accused surrendered the vehicle to the complainant on 14.10.2023.
Therefore the complainant company has auctioned the vehicle in as is where is basis and sold the vehicle to the highest bidder in the market on 29.11.2023.
After sale of the vehicle, the complainant company has adjusted the proceeds of the same to its loan outstanding and inspite of it, the complainant suffered loss on sale,
It is stated that the complainant has issued post sale notice dated 15.04.2024 calling the accused to clear the loss on sale of dues.
That under said contract, a sum of Rs.10,98,845/- was due and payable by the accused towards loss on sale of assets.

It is pleaded that towards discharge of the liability, the accused issued a cheque bearing No.044392 dated 03.06.2024 for a sum of Rs.10,98,845/-
drawn on Union Bank of India, Kanaswadi branch, Bengaluru.
The complainant presented said cheque for realization through its banker i.e. Standard Chartered Bank, Koramangala Branch, Bengaluru.
The said cheque returned dishonored on 04.06.2024 for the reason "Funds Insufficient".
Therefore the complainant got issued legal notice dated 03.07.2024 calling upon the accused to pay the amount covered in the cheque.
The notice was duly served on the accused on 09.07.2024.
Inspite of service of notice, the accused failed to pay the claim amount to the complainant within the statutory time.
Therefore, the accused has committed the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable C.C.No.25683/2024 Instruments Act.
Therefore the complainant has filed the complaint.

3. On the basis of Private complaint filed by the complainant, this court taken cognizance of offence and registered the case in PCR No.10695/2024 and recorded sworn statement of the authorised officer of the complainant as PW 1 and got marked 7 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.
This court by considering the material on record issued process under Section 227 of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita by registering the criminal case.
In response to the process issued by this court,

sentences.text: 3 9. POINT NO.1:
To prove the case the authorized representative of the complainant examined as PW- 2 and in his evidence affidavit he has reiterated the averments made in the complaint.
He has deposed that complainant is a non banking financial company incorporated under Companies Act and licenced by RBI.
The complainant is doing its business of providing credit facility to the borrowers for purchase of commercial vehicles.

To prove the incorporation of the company,
complainant has produced the web copy of the Incorporation Certificate as Ex.P 1.
The complainant has also produced company information registered in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs as Ex.P.14.
These documents prove the legal status of the complainant company.
The accused has not disputed the legal status of the C.C.No.25683/2024 complainant company.
The complainant has produced the true copies of the resolution of Board of Directors of the company as Ex.P 2 and Ex.P 8.
As per Ex.P 2 resolution, the Board of Directors of the company authorized PW 1 to file the complaint and to represent the complainant and to do all such acts detailed in the resolution.
Similarly as per Ex.P 8 resolution the Board of Directors of the company authorized PW 2 to file the complaint and to represent the complainant and to do all such acts detailed in the resolution.
The accused has denied the authority of PW 1 and PW 2 to represent the complainant company.
In the cross examination of PW 2 the accused has stated that Ex.P8 is a created document for the purpose of the case.
On perusal of Ex.P.8, it is the true copy of the Board Resolution passed in the meeting held on 23.03.2020 and the Company Secretary Alka Mishra issued the certified copy on 20.08.2021.
Ex.P 2 is the Board Resolution authorizing Nimi Nair to represent the company.
The accused has denied the authority of Alka Mishra to certify the Board Resolution.
But, Ex.P.14 shows that Alka Mishra is the Company Secretary as per the records maintained by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Ex.P 8 is the true copy of the Board Resolution passed on 29.10.2021 and certified and issued by the Company Secretary on 03.11.2021.
In the cross examination PW 2 has deposed that Nimi Nair is the Legal Manager and he is the Collection C.C.No.25683/2024 Support Executive.

He has deposed that therefore even though he had authorization as on the date of filing of the complaint to represent the complainant, Nimi Nair being the Senior officer in the company she has filed the complaint.

10. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the accused placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2015 (2) KCCR 1476 (George Joseph & Anr Vs HMT International Limited & Anr).

entities.text: 2015 (2) KCCR 1476 (George Joseph & Anr Vs HMT International Limited & Anr)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case the Honble High Court has observed that "The Articles of Association of the company did not confer the power on the Directors to sue or defend any proceedings on behalf of the company, the delegation of such power can only be by a Resolution of Board of Directors.

Hence a letter of authorization or power of attorney executed by the Chairman or other officers of the company without delegation of the power to institute such proceedings having emanated from the Board of Directors would invalidate any proceedings brought without the necessary authority".

The principles laid down in this decision is not applicable to the facts of the case on hand as the PW 1 and 2 are representing before this court on the basis of the Resolution of the Board of Directors as per ExP.2 and Ex.P.8 and they are not representing the case on the basis of the letter of authority C.C.No.25683/2024 executed by the directors or any other officer as found in the above referred decision.

15. It is now necessary to consider whether the complainant has complied statutory requirements for commission of the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

The C.C.No.25683/2024 essential ingredients of section 138 and 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act to be complied are i) drawing of the cheque by the accused ii) presentation of the cheque to the bank with in the period of three months, iii) returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank iv) giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque demanding of the payment of cheque amount with in the period of 30 days, v) failure of the drawer to make payment within the period of 15 days after receipt of the demand notice and v) Presentation of the complaint within a month by the complainant after expiry of 15 days of service of notice to the accused.
16.
The cheque is dated 03.06.2024.
It is dishonored on 04.06.2024 for the reason "Funds Insufficient".
The legal notice is dated 03.07.2024.
The notice duly served on the accused on 09.07.2024.

As provided under Section 146 of Negotiable Instruments Act, law presumes that on production of banker slip or memo having thereon the official mark denoting that the cheque has been dishonored, presume the fact of dishonor of such said cheque, unless and until same is disproved.
17.

But, he has not denied the receipt of postal consignment sent as per Ex.P.6 and he has not disputed the address mentioned in the legal notice.
If the postal consignment received by the accused does not contain Ex.P.5, the legal notice, he should have produced the letter/ document which is found in said postal consignment.

sentences.text: Therefore, the contention of the accused that the legal notice is not served on him cannot be accepted.
The accused has not issued any reply to the legal notice.
The PW 2 has deposed that inspite of service of notice, the accused failed to pay the claim amount to the complainant with in the statutory time of 15 days.
The cause of action for prosecution arose on expiry of 15 days of service of notice on 24-07-2024.
The complaint is filed before this court on 07.08.2024, within a month of cause of action.
The cheque is presented through the account of the complainant with Standard Chartered Bank, Koramangala Branch, which is situated with in the jurisdiction of this court.
The accused has not disputed that cheque is drawn from his account and also not disputed the signature on the cheque and not disputed issuance of cheque to the C.C.No.25683/2024 complainant.
The accused has also not disputed the dishonour of the cheque.
Thus the complainant has complied all the statutory requirements for constitution of offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
The accused has only denied the liability and contended that cheque is issued for security at the time of availment of the loan.
Therefore, the complainant is entitled for presumption under 118 and under Section 139 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

The provisions of Section 118 provides for presumption as to negotiable Instruments which reads as follows - 118- Presumptions as to negotiable Instruments - Until the contrary is proved, the following presumptions shall be made - (a) of consideration - that every negotiable Instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, indorsed,
negotiated or transferred, was accepted, indorsed, negotiated or transferred, was accepted, indorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration;
(b) as to date - that every negotiable instrument bearing a date was made or drawn on such date; (c) ..................
The provisions of Section 139 of Negotiable Instrument Act reads as under:-
139- Presumption in favour of holder - It should be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque, of the nature referred to in C.C.No.25683/2024 section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
18.

sentences.text: The accused has also relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in a decision reported in (2010) 11 SCC 411 between Rangappa V/s Sri Mohan has held that - The presumption mandated by Section 139 of the act does indeed include the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability.

It is also observed that Section 139 of the Act is an example of a reverse onus clause that has been included in furtherance of the legislative objective of improving the credibility of negotiable instrument.

It is also held that in such a C.C.No.25683/2024 scenario, the test of proportionality should guide the construction and interpretation of reverse onus clauses and the defendant caused cannot be expected to discharge an unduly high slandered or proof.

In this case,
the complainant is the financial company having valid licence from the RBI.

The accused has also not disputed availment of loan.
Therefore, the principles laid down in this decision is not helpful to the accused to support his arguments.

This court has gone through the principles laid down in the said decision and taken into consideration while appreciating the facts of the case.

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down in these decisions once the complainant has made out all the ingredients of Section 138 and 142 of N I Act and proved issuance of cheque by the accused and it is drawn from the account of the accused, the onus shifts on the accused to rebut the presumption under Section 118 and 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

In the above referred decisions, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has also laid down the principles how to appreciate the evidence while considering the aspect of rebuttal of the presumption by applying the principles of preponderance of probabilities.

Taking C.C.No.25683/2024 into consideration these legal aspects,

The accused has also not adduced his evidence or any witnesses on his behalf.

Therefore, the defence of the accused and rebuttal of the presumption is to be ascertained from the facts elicited from the mouth of PW 2 during cross examination.

It is also admitted fact that the accused purchased commercial Eicher vehicle from the Volvo and the accused approached the complainant for finance.

28. Another defence of the accused is that he has surrendered the vehicle to the complainant.
The complainant has auctioned the vehicle and appropriated the sale proceeds to the loan account and there is no balance to be paid by the accused to the complainant.
Therefore, the contention of the accused is that there is no legally recoverable debt payable to the complainant after appropriating the sale proceeds to the loan account.

In the Ex.P.13, statement of accounts a sum of Rs.14,75,000/-
is credited to the loan account on 29.11.2023 through cheque No.685805 Receipt No.257884.
The contention of the accused is that the complainant has shown lesser amount as sale proceeds than the actual sale proceeds received by the complainant.
In this regard in the cross examination of PW 2, it is elicited that " We have received sale proceeds in the auction of Rs.14,75,000/-.
For the sale proceeds we have paid CGST and SGST for Rs.79,017.86 each and it is given as debit entry in the statement of accounts.
I have not produced any documents supporting these entries dated 29.11.2023 before C.C.No.25683/2024 this court".
It is also elicited that "I have not produced details of auction held in respect of vehicle of accused.

While appreciating this defence of the accused, the court is required C.C.No.25683/2024 to appreciate the evidence considering the aspect whether this defence is in rebuttal to the presumption under Section 118 and 139 of N I Act.

As per the ratio laid down in the above referred decisions of Hon'ble Apex court, the complainant cannot be called upon to prove his case with cogent evidence beyond reasonable doubt till the accused is able to rebut the presumption with probable evidence.
Therefore in the light of these aspects, we have to consider this defence of the accused.
It is pertinent to note that the vehicle purchased in the month of September, 2022.

It is sold in auction on 29.11.2023.

Therefore without producing or eliciting anything from the mouth of PW 2 about the condition of the vehicle at the time of surrender, mere suggestion of the accused that the complainant C.C.No.25683/2024 has not accounted correct sale proceeds in the statement of account is a vague defence.
Mere suggestion is not sufficient to create a reasonable doubt in the mind of prudent person that the sale proceeds shown in the statement of account is not correct.
The accused has not made any efforts either to summon the auction proceedings or the valuation report obtained by the complainant to prima facie substantiate his defence.

Till the accused is not able to establish his defence with probable evidence and not able to rebut the presumption under Section 118 and 139 of N.I.Act, the complainant is having support of presumption of law and he cannot be called upon to prove existence of legally recoverable debt with cogent evidence.

In view of the explanation given by PW 2 for the debit entries made in the statement of accounts, there is no doubtful circumstances of making un-accounted debit entries is not made out by the accused.
Therefore, this defence of the accused that the complainant has made unaccounted debit entries in the statement of accounts and made exorbitant claim against the accused cannot be acceptable defence.
Therefore this court C.C.No.25683/2024 holds that this defence of the accused is also not helpful to the accused to create a reasonable doubt about existence of legally recoverable debt.
32. The accused has also taken defence that he has issued Ex.P.3, the cheque to the complainant at the time of sanction of loan amount for the purpose of security.
The complainant has also admitted that they have received blank signed cheque from the accused as per Ex.P.3 at the time of obtaining the loan documents.

In this regard the learned counsel for the complainant has drawn attention of this court to Schedule IV of the loan agreement marked as Ex.P.12.
In Schedule IV, there is entry about receiving several post dated cheques from the accused which includes Ex.P.3, the cheque in question.

In the said Schedule there is an specific authorization to the complainant to utilize the cheques which reads as under:
"We agree and acknowledge that any cheques that being delivered for the purpose of payment of EMIs are pursuant to our express request for payment of EMI through this mode of payment and the lender has informed us about its performance for NACH and has not insisted for payment of EMI through post dated cheques.

We agree and acknowledge that in accordance with provisions of Section 20 of the N.I.Act, the lender in the C.C.No.25683/2024 present case as the holder of the said cheques shall have authority to complete said cheques.

We agree and acknowledge that any dishonoring of any of the said cheques would make us liable including under the provisions of Section.138 of the Act, unless the amounts are paid within the notice period stipulated under said section given by the lender to us".

Thus, as per the terms of the agreement, the accused has authorized the complainant to complete the instrument under the provisions of Section 20 of N I Act and make use of such instrument for recovery of due amount in the loan account.

33. In this aspect it is proper to place on record the reliance to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court reported in (2022) 18 SCC 614 between Sripati Singh(since Dead) through his son Vs State of Jharkhand and another.
Wherein it is held that - 21.
A Cheque issued as security pursuant to a financial transaction cannot be considered as a worthless piece of paper under every circumstance.
"security" is something given as a pledge of payment.
It is given, deposited or pledged to make certain the fulfillment of an obligation to which the parties to the transaction are bound.

If in a transaction, a loan is advanced and the borrower M/S Volvo Financial Services (India) ... vs Bylappa N B on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117245815/
13 agrees to repay the C.C.No.25683/2024 amount in a specified time frame and issues a cheque as security to secure such repayment; if the loan amount is not repaid in any other form before the due date or if there is no other understanding or agreement between the parties to defer the payment of amount, the cheque which is issued as security would mature for presentation and the drawee of the cheque would be entitled to present the same.

sentences.text: On such presentation, if the same is dishonoured, the consequences contemplated under Section 138 and the other provisions of the NI Act would flow.
Therefore in view of the principles laid down in this decision, the cheque issued for security may also mature for presentation and on dishonour of the same the consequences under NI Act will follow.

Therefore in view of the terms of the agreement Ex.P.12 and the ratio laid down in this decision, only for the reason that the Ex.P 3 cheque was issued by the accused for security purpose itself does not disentitle the complainant to present it for securing legal liability.

Therefore, the contention of the accused that the complainant has misused the cheque issued for security cannot be accepted and it will not aid the C.C.No.25683/2024 accused to rebut the legal presumption under Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

34. Therefore, upon considering entire evidence placed on record, it can be safely concluded that there is no material on record to substantiate the defence and to rebut the presumption under Sec.139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore, there is no probable evidence is placed by the accused to rebut the presumption of existence of legally recoverable debt.

Therefore in view of the terms of the agreement Ex.P.12 and the ratio laid down in this decision, only for the reason that the Ex.P 3 cheque was issued by the accused for security purpose itself does not disentitle the complainant to present it for securing legal liability.
Therefore, the contention of the accused that the complainant has misused the cheque issued for security cannot be accepted and it will not aid the C.C.No.25683/2024 accused to rebut the legal presumption under Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
34. Therefore, upon considering entire evidence placed on record, it can be safely concluded that there is no material on record to substantiate the defence and to rebut the presumption under Sec.139 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore, there is no probable evidence is placed by the accused to rebut the presumption of existence of legally recoverable debt.
The complainant has complied the statutory requirements for constituting offence.
37. The Ho'ble High Court of Karnataka in the reportable decision in CRL.RP No. 996 of 2016 dated 09-07-2025 between M/s Banavathy and Company VS Mahaveer Electro Mech (P) Ltd at para 21 has held that - 21.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The Amount covered under the cheque is Rs.10,98,845/-.
Therefore considering these aspects it is appropriate to levy fine of Rs.12,52,190/- on the accused.
In case lesser interest is awarded and only default sentence is imposed, the rigor of offence under Section 138 will be diluted and thereby the object of the Statute will be defeated.
If recovery and compensatory part is not taken care of while determining the quantum of sentence and appropriate interest is not awarded, until the date of recovery of the entire amount, the complainant will be forced to file civil suit on the same subject matter.
In view of Section 143(3) the trial for offence M/S Volvo Financial Services (India) ... vs Bylappa N B on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117245815/
14 under Section 138 of N.I.Act has to be completed within six months.
If the said provision is not adhered to and the trial for the offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act takes 4 to 5 years, in the mean time, the claim of the complainant for recovery of the cheque amount by filing civil suit becomes barred by limitation.
Not only that the accused who is convicted for offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act challenges the same before the Sessions Court wherein the matter takes 2 to 3 years.
The accused unsuccessful in the said appeal prefers revision petition before the High Court and it is seen that the disposal of revision takes more than 5 years.
After all this if the complainant has to receive the fine/compensation as awarded by the trial Court, if it is cheque amount or little higher than the cheque amount, he will be at loss and put to injustice.
Therefore, while passing C.C.No.25683/2024 the order of sentence after determining the fine/compensation, the Court shall also pass an order to pay future interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount payable to the complainant by fixing time of one/two months to deposit compensation amount so that even if the matter is challenged before the Sessions Court in appeal and High Court in revision the interest of the complainant will be protected.
In view of the directions issued in the above refereed judgment, it is also proper to direct the accused to pay future interest on the fine amount at the rate of 9 % P.A. till payment.
Therefore considering all these aspects this court proceed to pass the following - ORDER By exercising powers conferred U/sec.278(2) of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita the accused is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.12,52,190/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand One Hundred & Ninety Only ) with in a month and in default accused shall pay interest at the rate of 9% from this day till payment of fine amount, and in default to pay the fine, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment of 6 months.
Further acting U/s 395(1)(a) of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Snhita out of the fine amount a sum of Rs.5,000/-
C.C.No.25683/2024 (Rupees Five Thousand Only) shall be defrayed as prosecution expenses to the state.
Further acting U/s 395(1)(b) of Bharathiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita a sum of Rs.12,47,190/-
(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Seven Thousand One Hundred & Ninety Only ) and interest out of the fine amount on recovery shall be paid as compensation to the complainant.
The bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall stands cancelled.
